summary: First testing pass of 'Long Distance Couples Photobooth'. Backend REST endpoints (create/get session) fully pass (8/8 pytest). Full happy-path E2E flow tested with two isolated Playwright browser contexts using an injected canvas-based fake getUserMedia stream (the environment's browser automation tool does not expose --use-fake-device-for-media-stream launch args, so a JS-level fake camera shim was used instead): session creation -> host camera enable -> guest joins via link -> both_ready -> synchronized countdown broadcast to both sides -> automatic 3-round capture -> result screen on both sides -> preview dialog -> retake resets both to both_ready -> guest disconnect correctly shows abandoned-state on host. Invalid join code and direct visit to nonexistent room code both correctly show error/not-found states. Mobile viewport (390x844) correctly stacks the camera video and partner-status-panel vertically. Code review of session_manager.py/server.py/photo_strip.py confirms no DB/disk persistence anywhere - captures dict is discarded (session.captures = {1:{},2:{},3:{}}) immediately in finalize_strip's finally block right after the strip is generated, and the data_url reference is deleted after broadcast.

ui_bugs.issue: Console warning: 'Missing Description or aria-describedby for DialogContent' - minor accessibility warning, not functionally blocking

action_items: Optional: add a DialogDescription (or aria-describedby) to the preview Dialog in ResultPanel.jsx to silence the Radix accessibility console warning.

Not a bug, but note for future testing agents: real getUserMedia via Playwright context.permissions alone did not succeed (no fake device flag support in this browser automation tool) - use a JS-injected canvas captureStream() shim (see context_for_next_testing_agent) for future camera-flow tests.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py / session_manager.py / photo_strip.py are clean, well-commented, and correctly scoped for the in-memory/no-persistence requirement.
finalize_strip() correctly discards session.captures in a finally block even on exception, and deletes the data_url reference after broadcasting - good privacy hygiene.
WebSocket flow (start_round_countdown -> schedule_capture -> handle_message photo_captured -> finalize_strip) correctly handles round progression and guards against stale round numbers.

Minor: handle_disconnect sets state to 'abandoned' but doesn't clear camera_ready flags on the disconnecting participant's server-side record; on reconnect this is recomputed correctly via both_camera_ready() so no functional bug, just noting for awareness.
No hardcoded URLs found; REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL and buildWsUrl() correctly derive ws/wss scheme.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows passed (happy path, invalid code, not-found, abandonment, mobile layout, retake)

test_credentials: None required - no auth in this app
seed_data_creation: None - test sessions created via POST /api/sessions and cleaned up naturally (in-memory, TTL-based)
context_for_next_testing_agent: Camera-flow E2E testing requires injecting a fake getUserMedia via context.add_init_script before page.goto, e.g. a canvas.captureStream() based MediaStream, since this environment's browser automation tool doesn't support --use-fake-device-for-media-stream Chromium launch flags. Full happy path (2 contexts, host+guest, 3 rounds, result, retake, abandonment) was verified working with this approach. Download button click was not verified to trigger an actual OS-level file save (code review shows a straightforward anchor with .download attribute pointing at the base64 data URL, which is standard practice and should work).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - no blocking bugs found. Only a low-priority Radix Dialog accessibility console warning (missing aria-describedby) was observed, purely cosmetic/console noise, no user-facing impact.
